direct: NGINX Open Source and Plus from 1.9.5 with HTTP/2 can be made to run code as the nginx worker without a login; fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and proof-of-concept code is public for one flaw.
downstream: Xint chained one flaw with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root and escape a Docker container, so a web front end can become a host compromise.
NGINX is embedded in load balancers, Kubernetes ingress controllers and appliances that update on their vendors' schedules, so exposure outlasts your own patching.
watch_for: Ingress and appliance vendors shipping fixed NGINX builds
Worker crashes on HTTP/2 traffic
A Linux kernel fix and CVE for the SCTP flaw
Reports of in-the-wild exploitation

direct: PLAID suspended all KARTE services after unauthorized access on Nov 13; account emails and integration credentials are listed as leaked, along with part of the data customers imported.
downstream: DHC says about 19.11 million customer records and BASE FOOD about 710,000 customers' names and emails leaked through KARTE.
Integration credentials held by the service may open customers' own systems, and leaked customer lists feed targeted phishing in Japanese.
watch_for: Further KARTE customers announcing leaks
Phishing that uses shop names and dates of birth
Use of integration keys connected to KARTE

direct: Any service that decodes untrusted Base64 on an affected x86-64 HotSpot Java runtime could be crashed or taken over without a login.
downstream: Java is bundled inside third-party applications, appliances and container images, so exposure extends to products you did not build.
Patching depends on each vendor shipping an updated runtime, so some systems will stay exposed after your own servers are fixed.
watch_for: Unexpected JVM crashes and restarts
Vendor advisories naming a bundled Java runtime
Signs of exploitation reported by CISA or vendors

direct: Self-hosted Confluence Data Center with the Remote API enabled can be taken over without a login; CISA lists the Axis flaw as exploited.
downstream: In the case Rapid7 saw, the intruder took database credentials, queried a cloud data warehouse and signed in to Microsoft 365 as a service account.
Apache Axis 1.x is end-of-life and may sit inside other Java products that will not get a fix.
watch_for: Unusual Remote API requests to Confluence
Service accounts signing in from new places
Other products bundling Apache Axis 1.x

direct: Internet-facing N-central servers were exploited through zero-days published without coordinated disclosure; crypto miners were deployed.
downstream: An RMM server reaches every managed client, so a compromise can spread to many customer networks at once.
Removal of the Legacy API may break older integrations that still depend on it.
watch_for: N-central servers not on Hotfix 3
New agents or scripts pushed from RMM
Mining processes on managed endpoints

direct: Account and billing data for every Fireworks AI account created before Oct 30 was exposed; some customers' secrets, model files and datasets were reached earlier.
downstream: Cursor, Notion and Uber are reported as affected customers; keys held by the provider led to a trojanized extension at Cursor.
Credentials pasted into AI prompts or held by inference providers can open systems far from the provider itself.
watch_for: Notices from AI and inference providers you use
Use of API keys issued to providers
Secrets in AI chat logs and traces

direct: Malicious JavaScript was injected into some Optimizely Web Experimentation customer projects, reaching 178 organisations by one researcher's count.
downstream: Coverage says the code skimmed payment cards and swapped crypto addresses on customers' sites, so their visitors were the victims.
Sites that load third-party scripts without integrity checks or a strict Content-Security-Policy inherit the supplier's compromise.
watch_for: Unexpected scripts on checkout pages
CSP violation reports
Notices from script and tag vendors

direct: Saved payee records at about 40 Irish credit unions were exposed through a reported attack on supplier Wellington IT using valid credentials and an authorization flaw.
downstream: Payee data can be used to make fraud and impersonation messages to members more convincing.
A minister called the six-week delay in telling credit unions unacceptable, so expect regulatory scrutiny of supplier notification.
watch_for: Payment-redirection and impersonation lures to members
Statements from the supplier or the Central Bank
Automated API abuse with valid logins

direct: Six unpatched pre-authentication flaws let attackers take over Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers; hundreds are reachable online.
downstream: Food retail, cold storage and pharmacies risk spoiled stock and safety incidents; French attacks on such controllers were linked to fires.
France is seeking EU sanctions over the campaign, which could prompt further attacks or warnings.
watch_for: Refrigeration controllers reachable from the internet
Unexpected setpoint or alarm changes
CVE numbers and fixes from Danfoss

direct: Equinor's IT systems are under an ongoing attack; it says production is unaffected and email was reported down.
downstream: Restoration time is unknown, so partners and suppliers may see delays or unusual messages from Equinor.
Attackers often use a known incident to send fake invoices or updates in the victim's name.
watch_for: Messages claiming to come from Equinor
Norwegian authority advisories
Any named attacker or leak claim
